text:
Something rises from the flat, dry land ahead. At first it looks like a rock — another one of the strange formations that break the horizon here. But it does not look like a rock. The shape is wrong. Too smooth. Too deliberate.

It is tall. Rounded, tapering toward the top like a seed or a shell, half-buried in the sand as though it grew there, or fell there long ago. The surface is pale brown, warm-hued in the daylight. Oval openings break the face of it — dark, and silent, except for one near the base, where something glows faintly. Amber. Warm.

A thin trickle of dark water winds from its base and loses itself in the dust.

The red-leafed trees off to one side are still. Nothing moves.
The strange structure waits at the edge of the flats, same as before. The amber glow from the lower opening is visible even from here. The trickle of dark water at its base catches the light.

The land around it is flat and dry, broken only by scattered scrub and the long shadows of distant mesas. No paths lead here — not worn ones, anyway. No signs of passage. Whatever this place is, it does not announce itself.

The smell is mineral. Hot stone and something faintly smoky, carried on the dry air from within.

That glow again. Low down, near the ground. Patient.

Up close, the surface is smoother than it looked from a distance. Not carved — or not carved in any way that left marks. The material is warm beneath the fingers. Dense. Old.

The openings above are dark. The one at ground level is not. A soft amber light breathes from inside — oil, maybe, or something slower. The opening is wide enough to walk through. There is no door.

Something is in there.

You press your knuckles to the surface and knock.

The sound carries strangely — a low, hollow resonance, as if the structure is not solid all the way through.

A pause. Then, from somewhere inside, soft footsteps.

You lean toward the opening and call out.

Your voice feels oddly flat in the dry air. No echo from the structure — it seems to swallow the sound.

A pause. Then, from somewhere inside, soft footsteps.
You knock. Almost immediately — soft footsteps from within.
You knock. The same low resonance as before. A pause. Then footsteps.
You walk up to the structure. The amber glow from the lower opening is steady, warm. The surface is the same — smooth, old, still warm from the day's heat.
You turn back toward the open land.
